scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8876: host_1_1_1_1 (10.1.1.2) reports it cannot reach
anything outside its own subnet -- no server farm, no other pod, and name
lookups time out too. It can still ping its gateway address 10.1.1.1.
host_2_1_1_1 is unaffected and reaches everything normally. Diagnose
host_1_1_1_1's connectivity.

injection.action: point the host's default route at a non-existent in-subnet gateway
injection.command:
ip route del default 2>/dev/null
  ip route add default via 10.1.1.254

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: host_1_1_1_1 default-gateway configuration
Mechanism: host_1_1_1_1's correct gateway is 10.1.1.1 (switch_dist_1_1's br0
  address). Its default route was repointed to 10.1.1.254 -- in-subnet but
  unassigned -- so ARP for the gateway never resolves and no off-subnet
  packet leaves the host. On-link destinations (10.1.1.1 via the connected
  route) still work, which is why the gateway pings fine. DNS "times out"
  only because the resolver 10.200.0.2 is off-subnet. The network itself is
  healthy: pod 2 reaches everything, and switch_dist_1_1 still advertises
  10.1.1.0/24.
Localization: host_1_1_1_1
Root cause: host_1_1_1_1's default gateway set to 10.1.1.254 instead of
  10.1.1.1
Fix: restore the default route on host_1_1_1_1 --
  `ip route replace default via 10.1.1.1 dev eth0`
scenario.fix_spec:
restore host_1_1_1_1's default route --
`ip route replace default via 10.1.1.1 dev eth0`
scoring_axes: must-identify-component: default gateway / default route points at wrong address (10.1.1.254 instead of 10.1.1.1)
bonus-exonerates-network: notes switch_dist_1_1 and the OSPF core are healthy (pod 2 works, the real gateway answers), so no network device needs fixing

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is a misconfigured default gateway on host_1_1_1_1. The host
has its default route set to 10.1.1.254, but no device in the topology
owns that address. The actual Layer-3 gateway for the 10.1.1.0/24 subnet
is switch_dist_1_1, whose bridge interface br0 carries 10.1.1.1/24.

Because 10.1.1.254 is inside the host's own subnet (10.1.1.0/24), the
kernel attempts to ARP-resolve it directly rather than rejecting it
immediately. That ARP request goes unanswered, leaving the ARP entry
permanently "incomplete." Every packet destined for any address outside
10.1.1.0/24 — web servers, the DNS server, the peer pod — is handed to
the kernel's default route, which stalls waiting for an ARP reply that
never arrives, producing "Destination Host Unreachable" ICMP errors back
to the host itself. Meanwhile, 10.1.1.1 (the real gateway) is perfectly
reachable because it IS present and ARP-resolves normally, explaining why
the host can ping its gateway while everything else fails.

The comparison host, host_2_1_1_1, uses 10.2.1.1 as its default gateway,
which correctly matches switch_dist_2_1's br0 address — hence full
connectivity there.

Root cause: host_1_1_1_1's startup configuration sets the default gateway
to 10.1.1.254 instead of the correct 10.1.1.1.

Corrective fix: On host_1_1_1_1, remove the stale route
(`ip route del default via 10.1.1.254`) and install the correct one
(`ip route add default via 10.1.1.1 dev eth0`). Permanently fix the
Kathara startup file for host_1_1_1_1 to use gateway 10.1.1.1.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly names host_1_1_1_1 as the source of the misconfigured default gateway (a host-side issue).

Removes the wrong default and adds the correct default via 10.1.1.1 (and updates startup), which matches the expected fix.

The agent's logs show the live route, gateway IPs, successful pings to 10.1.1.1, failed ARP/resolution for 10.1.1.254, and empty startup files; the diagnosis that the host's default route points at an unassigned in-subnet address and thus blocks off-subnet traffic follows logically.
